References to data found in the code of audioOS 27 indicate that Apple is developing multiple new HomePod features. The code appears to show Apple is working on a brand-new surround sound system, a feature called "Party Mode," and more.

HomePod New Features Are in the Works

These codes were discovered by a MacRumors forum user this week in audioOS 27 beta 8.

The most notable mention is that the code references support for configuring four full-size HomePods (second generation) into a surround sound system. Currently, HomePod supports pairing into a stereo pair as the default audio output for Apple TV.

Within this four-speaker configuration, each speaker has a dedicated role and audio processing. The front speakers use dedicated processing technology, responsible for left and right channels, and will compensate for situations where the speakers might be close to a wall or corner. The rear HomePods adopt omnidirectional audio processing, designed to fill the space behind and around the listener. The new tuning settings include a program that manages the bass and treble units of each HomePod, and controls bass, EQ, sound synchronization, and calibration data.

The code also mentions dynamic surround sound audio tuning functionality. This feature would allow the four-HomePod system to automatically adjust audio processing based on playback content (such as movies or music).

The code also references a new system called "Forklift." "Forklift" appears to combine two full-size second-generation HomePods with two additional speakers of an unknown model—the identification codes of those two speakers do not match any existing Apple HomePod product.

Bloomberg previously reported that Apple may launch an all-new HomePod mini in the coming months. The company is also "testing a new full-size HomePod," but that product is not ready for release in the short term. Apple's existing full-size HomePod was launched in February 2023.

Another new feature is called "Party Mode." According to the code, once Party Mode is enabled, the HomePod's sound will "spread out into a wider, more spacious mix" in order to "evenly fill the room, rather than creating a perfect listening position in front of the speaker."

It remains unknown whether Apple will ultimately release these features. However, it is encouraging to see that Apple is still committed to upgrading the HomePod lineup's home theater capabilities.
